key_insight: THz time-domain spectroscopy can non-destructively fingerprint specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films by matching distinct terahertz absorption modes to defect species.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, room-temperature diagnostic for closed-loop defect detection and passivation in perovskite solar-cell manufacturing.
method: Measure 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of sequential-vacuum-evaporated perovskite films.
Identify intrinsic phonon modes and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations for multiple compositions.
Use oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and build a THz fingerprint library.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting quantitative defect metrology.
watch_item: The approach depends on a well-constructed material-specific THz library and may need calibration to separate overlapping spectral features across different perovskite compositions.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
